title: Keyvalue window edge-case: sticky offsets & kernel selection scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad while bisecting a long-context regression that shows up when sequence length > 32k tokens for some sessions. Goal: capture commands, error snippets, temporary hypotheses, minimal repros, and next steps so I don't forget between pre-meetings and stack traces.

Short summary of symptom:
- Intermittent model stalls (hangs on token generation) observed starting 2025-01-20 after the attention kernel selector changes in runtime v2.9.3.
- Failure only reproducible for long contexts (approx > 30k tokens) and certain session patterns (prefix-heavy, frequent partial-flush).
- When issue triggers, subsequent requests from same session show mismatched KV offsets (future attention reading from wrong slot) -> incoherent completion or repeat tokens.

What I saw (console logs / snippets):
- Runtime log excerpt (INFO + debug lines):
  [2025-01-24T14:12:08Z] session=abcd1234 length=33240 selected_kernel=flash_attn_v2
  [2025-01-24T14:12:08Z] kv_cache: write_offset=32768 read_offset=16384 last_flush=2025-01-24T14:11:55Z
  [2025-01-24T14:12:08Z] attention: computed_offsets -> {layer3: 0x7f8a1234, layer4: 0x7f8a9abc}
  [2025-01-24T14:12:08Z] ERROR: attention mismatch detected: read_slot 32768 != expected 16384 (layer4)

- In one repro run I saw a CUDA error before the mismatch:
  CUDA ERROR 700: unspecified launch failure (at kernel cutlass_gemm_sm80)
  followed by fallback to triton_dot (slower) and then flash_attn_v2 (fast) selected by selector.

Commands I used to reproduce locally:
- start local runtime with debug flags and long test playlist:
  RUNTIME_DEBUG=1 ./bin/redwood-runtime --config ./tests/long-context/config-32k.yaml --log-level=debug

- run client repro script (python):
  python tools/repro_long_context.py --session-file sessions/sess-abcd.json --seed 42 --target-len 33240 --stream

- save a trace of kernels selected:
  export KERNEL_TRACE=/tmp/kernel_trace.txt; tail -f /var/log/redwood/runtime.log | grep kernel >> $KERNEL_TRACE &

Observed kernel selection patterns (from trace):
- start -> cutlass_gemm_sm80, then cutlass_attention, then CUDA error, then selector triggers fallback-> triton_dot, then flash_attn_v2.
- In successful short sessions, selector picks flash_attn_v2 consistently.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kernel fallback ordering + partial KV flush creates inconsistent KV indexing: when a kernel fails and we switch mid-layer, the runtime's KV write pointer isn't advanced consistently across kernels (off-by-chunk). That leaves stale entries readable by later layers.
2) Some attention kernels assume contiguous KV layout (no wrap) while others accept circular buffer semantics; mixing them without normalization causes read_offset mismatch.
3) Long sequence/high offset causes integer wrap or signedness issue in some mapping (observed offsets near 32768, suspicious boundary).
4) Race between background prefix-caching thread and the main serving thread during partial session flush leading to ghosted entries.

Quick experiments I ran (and results):
- Force single kernel (flash_attn_v2) for all layers: no repro in 20 runs. Suggests selector behavior is implicated.
  command: ./bin/redwood-runtime --cfg-override "kernel.selector=force:flash_attn_v2"

- Force fallback-first (triton_dot) for layer 3 only: reproduced mismatch in 3/10 runs, but less frequently.

- Introduced aggressive KV pointer logging at write/read call sites (added dumps of pointer, epoch, and layer id): mismatch always shows write_epoch != read_epoch for failing sessions.

- Small repro to test wrap: wrote unit test that simulates circular buffer index arithmetic with +32768 additions; no overflow with 32-bit signed, but we use 16-bit in some indexing arrays (possible bug).

Minimal repro plan (next):
- Create synthetic session that performs: append 28k prefix tokens, then 4k shorter prefix flush operations, then send 1k regen. Try with deterministic seeds. Use kernel forcing toggles.
- Run under cuda-memcheck / cuda-gdb to capture kernel faults.
- Add byte-level dump of KV ring buffer after each write (for failing case only) and diff against successful run.

Immediate TODOs (short term):
- [ ] Add metric counters: kernel_switch_count/session, kv_epoch_increments, kv_wrap_events. (Evan)
- [ ] Add normalization step when switching kernel implementations: ensure both kernels see consistent conceptual offsets (Maya)
- [ ] Add assertions in runtime: if read_offset > write_offset + threshold -> dump and abort earlier with richer trace (Samir)
- [ ] Try reproducing with older runtime v2.8.x to confirm regression introduced in v2.9.3 (Evan)

Notes / stray observations:
- The failing sessions often have high number of user edits (prefix updates) in quick succession. Might be correlated with prefix-caching thread doing partial compaction.
- One dump showed a stale pointer to an evicted shard (evict happened but pointer not cleared). Look into eviction callback ordering.
- GPU type in CI repro hosts: A100s with driver 535.x; local dev box is also A100. Might be schedule/order differences on p4 vs a100.

Longer-term ideas (if this is systemic):
- Standardize an intermediate KV API that all kernels call into; kernel implementations only provide read/write ops but do not manage offsets themselves. Enforce one canonical offset advancement path.
- Add a test harness that fuzzes kernel switching with synthetic kernels that intentionally fail to stress selector fallbacks and KV consistency.

Notes for next sync with Maya (scheduled 2025-02-04):
- Bring kernel_trace + KV dumps from last 5 failing sessions.
- Show forced-single-kernel runs vs mixed-kernel failures.
- Discuss adding quick fix: on kernel switch, atomically snapshot offsets and validate per-layer ranges before continuing.

End of scratchpad. Will copy this into a GH comment on PR 1456 after repro runs that include cuda-gdb trace.

-- Evan
